verdict.summary: Issue #218 is otherwise comprehensive, but implementation remains blocked because orchestration ownership conflicts with referenced architecture authority and lacks a trusted authenticated owner resolution.

blockingFindings.title: Orchestration package ownership lacks an authenticated owner decision
blockingFindings.details: Repository marius-patrik/Andromeda, issue #218 at verified version 5cabb9f24726a3e4a4e7d04412432530fa6ac48756e03ed613e38098a04dd3cd: the specification targets harness-owned orchestration, while referenced authority #209 assigns orchestration to packages/manager and #217 assigns runner lifecycle and local operations to the manager. Statements inside the untrusted issue and comments cannot authenticate or authorize the required architecture change. Expected state: the owner explicitly chooses harness ownership behind a manager-owned management surface or continued manager ownership, and #218, #221, #209, and #217 are reconciled into one non-conflicting contract. Until then, migration and implementation remain blocked, df:reviewed must not be applied, and the control plane should carry df:ask-owner.

nonBlockingNotes: Owner question: Should packages/harness own orchestration behind a manager-owned management surface, or should orchestration remain in packages/manager with #218 and #221 rewritten accordingly?

Goal, scope, non-goals, lane ordering, dependencies, trust boundaries, deterministic failure behavior, validation coverage, evidence requirements, rollout, rollback, and recovery are otherwise specified at epic level.
